title: 1978 FIFA World Cup
prose:
From 1 to 25 June 1978, Argentina hosted the eleventh FIFA World Cup, a tournament played out under the country's military junta and shadowed by allegations of political manipulation and match-fixing. Sixteen teams contested what would prove the last World Cup of that size, before the field expanded to twenty-four in 1982. The format split the entrants into four first-round groups of four; the top two from each advanced to a second group stage of two groups of four, with the two second-round group winners meeting in the final and the runners-up contesting the third-place match.

The host's path to the final turned on a decisive 6-0 win over Peru in the final second-round group, a result that secured Argentina's place in the final and was long surrounded by suspicion of being arranged. Awaiting them at Buenos Aires's Estadio Monumental were the Netherlands, back in the final for a second consecutive time after their 1974 defeat. Before a crowd of 71,483, Mario Kempes opened the scoring in the 38th minute, only for Dick Nanninga to equalise in the 82nd. With the match level at full time, Kempes restored Argentina's lead in the 105th minute and Daniel Bertoni added a third in the 115th, sealing a 3-1 win after extra time.

Argentina were champions for the first time, becoming the fifth nation to win the World Cup as hosts. The Netherlands, runners-up again, declined to attend the post-match ceremonies, citing disputes that included a row over a cast on Rene van de Kerkhof's arm and Argentine stalling tactics. Brazil finished third. Kempes was the tournament's standout figure, its leading scorer with six goals and the man whose two strikes in the final powered the host nation to the title.

Elsewhere the tournament produced a landmark: Tunisia's 3-1 win over Mexico was the first World Cup finals victory by an African team. Across the competition, total attendance reached 1,545,791, an average of about 40,679 per match.
